causal_chain: A small set of persistent user intent slots can preserve separable preference modes across the interaction history.
Event-conditioned transport between intent slots lets recent items reweight which latent mode is active without requiring session labels or held-out access.
Reduced mode averaging should improve ranking of held-out items, especially for users with diverse histories, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 than static single-vector collaborative filters.
Scoring candidates by the best-supported intent slot plus a disagreement penalty against conflicting slots reduces averaging over incompatible interests.
Users with mixed tastes are poorly summarized by a single static embedding.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain may come only from increased parameter count or regularization side effects rather than from multi-state transport and disagreement-aware routing.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating cross-slot transport while keeping multiple slots should reduce performance more than merely shrinking embedding dimension, indicating that dynamic routing rather than capacity alone matters.

Compared with a matched single-embedding control of similar parameter scale, the proposed model should show larger NDCG@10 improvement on users with longer or more diverse histories than on very short-history users.
The disagreement penalty should help ranking of substitute-like or niche positives that would otherwise be suppressed by averaging across incompatible user interests.
expected_evidence: Mechanism-off ablations can isolate the contribution of multi-slot memory, event-conditioned transport, and disagreement-aware scoring.
Qualification runs can compare the frontier candidate against a matched single-vector parent-equivalent control under the frozen ML-1M full-sort protocol.
User-stratified offline analysis by history length or item-diversity bins can test whether benefits concentrate on multi-interest users.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched single-embedding control with comparable parameter count matches or exceeds the candidate, and ablations removing transport or disagreement routing do not materially degrade ranking, the hypothesis that multi-state transport is the operative mechanism is falsified.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core user representation from one embedding to an explicit set of latent intent states, introduces learned transport dynamics over those states conditioned on observed items, and changes scoring to disagreement-aware intent routing. These are new representational and interaction semantics rather than a loss tweak, sampler swap, or propagation wrapper.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent intent states, updates those states through item-conditioned transport during train-time history encoding, and scores each candidate through disagreement-aware routing over the resulting state bank will outperform a matched static single-embedding collaborative filter on frozen ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 because it preserves separable user interests instead of collapsing them into one average preference vector.
implementation_requirements: Build train-only user history tensors from the frozen training interactions without touching validation or test data.
Define candidate scoring as max-or-softmax aggregation over slot-specific user-item affinities with a disagreement penalty from non-selected slots.
Encode each user's train history by recurrently applying an item-conditioned transport operator over the K slots.
Implement a new RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise loss and full-sort prediction methods.
Maintain K user intent slots and item embeddings in torch.
Provide an executable mechanism-off ablation that collapses K slots to one static user embedding while preserving the same training loop and evaluation interface.
Support deterministic offline qualification within the provided wall-clock and GPU budget.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched control implemented in the same candidate code path that removes multi-slot memory and transport, collapsing to a single static user embedding with the same item embeddings, pairwise loss family, optimizer family, and evaluation protocol.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace the single user representation with a multi-slot persistent intent memory, add item-conditioned transport between slots during history encoding, and score with disagreement-aware routing over slots rather than direct static dot-product only.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is an otherwise matched model that uses one static user embedding per user, no slot transport, no disagreement routing, and standard user-item dot-product scoring under the same pairwise training and full-sort evaluation interface.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Implement a 3-slot latent-intent transport recommender with train-history encoding from observed user sequences and compare it against the matched single-slot mechanism-off under identical ML-1M pairwise full-sort qualification.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does explicit multi-state user memory with item-conditioned transport and disagreement-aware routing improve NDCG@10 over a matched static single-embedding collaborative filter?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with small K and simple linear transport should fit within the qualification budget because ML-1M is modest in scale, train-history encoding is based only on training interactions, and the model can reuse efficient batched dot-product scoring for full-sort evaluation once user slot states are precomputed.
